This vignette walks through a complete reserving analysis: building
triangles from claim transactions, checking the data, estimating development
factors, running chain ladder, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, Cape Cod and Mack, and
comparing the results.

The data are **synthetic** (`claims_synthetic`, `premium_synthetic`) and do
not represent any insurer's experience.

```{r}
library(reservekit)
```

## Terminology

| Term | Meaning in reservekit |
|---|---|
| Origin period | Accident (or underwriting/report) period: the rows of a triangle. |
| Development age | Time since the start of the origin period: the columns. |
| Valuation date | The date of the latest diagonal. |
| Latest | The value on the latest diagonal for each origin. |
| Ultimate | Estimated final value of the origin's claims. |
| Reserve | Ultimate minus latest. On **paid** data this is total unpaid (case reserves + IBNR); on **incurred** data it is IBNR (including IBNER). |

## 1. Build triangles from claim transactions

`as_triangle()` needs to be told whether values are cumulative or
incremental; it never guesses.

```{r}
head(claims_synthetic)

paid <- as_triangle(claims_synthetic, origin = "accident_year",
                    development = "dev_age", value = "paid",
                    type = "incremental", measure = "paid", dev_step = 1)
incurred <- as_triangle(claims_synthetic, origin = "accident_year",
                        development = "dev_age", value = "incurred",
                        type = "incremental", measure = "incurred", dev_step = 1)
to_cumulative(paid)
```

Rules worth knowing:

* Several rows for one origin/age cell are **summed** for incremental data.
  For cumulative data duplicates are refused unless `aggregate = "sum"`.
* An incremental cell inside the observed region with no transactions is set
  to 0 and recorded (`attr(x, "filled")`). A missing cumulative cell is a
  **genuine missing value**, which fitting functions refuse.
* Cells beyond the latest diagonal are **structural** future values and are
  never confused with missing data.

## 2. Check the data

```{r}
validate_triangle(paid)
validate_triangle(raa)
```

Findings are graded `error` (fitting will stop), `warning` (needs review) and
`note` (legitimate features such as negative incurred development from case
reserve releases).

## 3. Development factors and tail

```{r}
dev_factors(paid)
dev_factors(paid, method = "simple", n_periods = 5)
dev_factors(paid, tail = "exponential")
```

Judgemental selections are explicit overrides and are recorded:

```{r}
dev_factors(paid, override = c("9-10" = 1.005), tail = 1.01)
```

## 4. Chain ladder

```{r}
cl <- fit_chain_ladder(paid, tail = "exponential")
cl
predict(cl, type = "incremental")
```

The projected increments of every origin add up exactly to its reserve.

## 5. Bornhuetter-Ferguson and Cape Cod

```{r}
prem <- premium_synthetic$earned_premium
bf <- fit_bf(paid, exposure = prem, elr = 0.65, tail = "exponential")
cc <- fit_cape_cod(paid, exposure = prem, tail = "exponential")
cc$elr
```

## 6. Mack chain ladder and reserve uncertainty

```{r}
mack <- fit_mack(paid)
summary(mack)
```

`se` is the square root of Mack's estimated **mean squared error of
prediction** (process + parameter error). It is not a confidence interval for
the mean, and no distribution is assumed: this version produces no
quantiles or prediction intervals. Mack fits do not take a tail factor in
this version.

```{r}
plot(mack)
```

## 7. Diagnostics

```{r}
d <- diagnostics(mack)
d$correlation
d$calendar
plot(mack, which = "residuals")
```

## 8. Compare methods

```{r}
compare_methods(chain_ladder = cl, bf = bf, cape_cod = cc)
```

`compare_methods()` does not pick a winner. Method selection remains an
actuarial judgement informed by the diagnostics, the data and knowledge of the
business.

## Paid versus incurred

```{r}
compare_methods(paid = fit_chain_ladder(paid), incurred = fit_chain_ladder(incurred),
                value = "ultimate")
```
